title: introduce-inference-economist-prefill-automation-and-quant-suggester
author: Maya Thompson
description: Context: tenants frequently accept our batching/caching defaults but still overspend because defaults are conservative or misaligned with traffic shape. This PR introduces the Inference Economist (codename 'CostCraft'), an on-node suggestion engine that generates tenant-specific prefill/batching/caching defaults and ranked quantization profiles based on a lightweight unit-econ estimator and short replay of recent traces. Motivation: reduce unit cost while preserving SLOs by providing safe, actionable defaults that can be auto-applied for new tenants or suggested in Console. Design summary: (1) Prefill autosuggestor: replays sampled recent traces (100-500 requests) in fast-sim mode to compute cost/latency tradeoffs across candidate batch sizes, prefill thresholds and KV caching windows; (2) Quant suggester: small ranking model + heuristics produce an ordered list of quantization profiles (fp16->q4_0->q4_1->int8 candidates) with an estimated quality penalty score and unit cost delta; (3) Budget-aware selector: tenant budget and latency SLOs are inputs; we compute a Pareto front and propose a default profile plus two safe fallbacks; (4) Telemetry & safety guards: propose-only by default, automatic apply behind a tenant opt-in flag; automatic rollback if tail latency or error-rate increases beyond thresholds in 10m window. Checklist: - [x] lightweight simulation harness implemented and unit-tested - [x] quant ranking model + model card + small calibration dataset - [x] telemetry events and Console proposal UI hooks - [x] e2e replay smoke tests added - [x] canary rollout plan documented in PR - [ ] docs/ops deep-dive (follow-up doc linked below). Backwards compatibility: runtime behavior unchanged unless tenant opt-in flag is enabled. Security & privacy: only uses per-tenant aggregated traces; no raw request payloads are persisted. Rollout plan: canary on 3 staging tenants -> gradual ramp to 10% of new tenants -> Console suggestion visible to all and auto-apply as opt-in tenant feature. Rollback: feature flag off will remove suggestions and scheduled jobs; runtime falls back to existing defaults. Related: ENG-3219 (prefill autosuggest), ENG-3380 (quant-ranker). More details in docs/quickstarts/costcraft.md and design notes in the PR thread.

feat(quant): add lightweight quant_ranking model and profile serializer
feat(cli): expose costcraft suggestions via 'rwd costcraft suggest'
chore(telemetry): add costcraft suggestion events and dashboard metrics
test(e2e): add replay-based smoke test and perf asserts
docs: add quickstart and rollout guide
review_thread: Jamal: Can the simulation harness run without touching GPU so it won't increase infra cost during canary?; Maya: Yes — the default mode is a 'fast-sim' that uses lightweight statistical modeling (no model forward passes) and runs on CPU; an opt-in full-sim mode can be enabled for deeper calibration.; Lena: The quant ranking model looks promising but we need a clear signal for quality regressions. Add a 'quality_penalty_estimate' to the profile and surface it in Console.; Maya: Added quality_penalty_estimate, plus an integration test that checks the penalty estimator against a small golden dataset.; Ravi: I'm concerned about autoscaling interactions. If suggestions increase batching, will autoscaler schedules be adjusted and could that cause cold-starts?; Maya: Added a guard that prevents suggested batch sizes that increase per-node CPU beyond 70% for Dedicated pools and added a note in canary runbook to observe scaling metrics.; Lena: Approving after fixes.; Jamal: Approving (comment: watch the downstream billing report).
merge_outcome: merged via squash by Maya Thompson on 2026-03-12; merge commit message: feat(econ): add inference economist (prefill autosuggest + quant suggester)
release_notes: Introduce 'Inference Economist' (CostCraft): tenant-specific prefill/batching/caching suggestions and ranked quantization profiles; opt-in by default with safe fallbacks; lightweight simulation harness for fast candidate scoring; telemetry and Console hooks for proposals and approvals; canary rollout controlled by feature-flag; no runtime change unless enabled.
